s01: Seven units can leave the source, and seven can enter the destination.
Yet this network can carry only six units per time step.
The limit is hiding between the endpoints.
Each arrow gives a direction and a capacity.
Flow cannot exceed that capacity, and intermediate junctions must pass on everything they receive.
Separate the source and junction A from the other two nodes.
Every route to the destination must cross this boundary.
Only three arrows cross forward: capacities three, one, and two.
Their total is six.
No routing can carry more than six across that cut.
Can we actually achieve six?
Send two along the route through A directly to the destination.
Send three through B.
Send one more through A, then B, then the destination.
Every capacity is respected, and flow balances at each junction.
We have both a limit of six and a routing that reaches six.
That proves this routing is optimal.
This is the idea behind the max flow, min cut theorem.
Now increase the middle arrow from one to two.
The cut can carry seven, and one extra unit can follow the middle route.
The network now achieves seven.
A useful improvement came from the constraint that was actually binding.

scenes.narration:
Seven units can leave the source, and seven can enter the destination. Yet this network can carry only six units per time step. The limit is hiding between the endpoints.

Each arrow gives a direction and a capacity. Flow cannot exceed that capacity, and intermediate junctions must pass on everything they receive. Separate the source and junction A from the other two nodes. Every route to the destination must cross this boundary.

Only three arrows cross forward: capacities three, one, and two. Their total is six. No routing can carry more than six across that cut.

Can we actually achieve six? Send two along the route through A directly to the destination. Send three through B. Send one more through A, then B, then the destination. Every capacity is respected, and flow balances at each junction.

We have both a limit of six and a routing that reaches six. That proves this routing is optimal. This is the idea behind the max flow, min cut theorem.

Now increase the middle arrow from one to two. The cut can carry seven, and one extra unit can follow the middle route. The network now achieves seven. A useful improvement came from the constraint that was actually binding.
